chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, from al-Kinānī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man and a woman who are found in one covering. He said: “Flog each of them one hundred lashes.” He said: “And stoning is not to take place until the four witnesses establish that they saw him having intercourse with her.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: The correct way to understand these reports is that, when the act is added to their being in one garment, and the Imam comes to know that from them, then at that point he establishes the full hadd upon them. And stoning does not take place except after the establishment of proof, in accordance with what is contained in the report of Abū Baṣīr and al-Kinānī. That which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.اجْلِدْهُمَا: inflict flogging upon both of them as a hadd punishment
key_terms.الرَّجْمُ: stoning as a prescribed punishment in the relevant legal context
key_terms.الشُّهُودُ الْأَرْبَعَةُ: the four witnesses required to establish the act for rajm
key_terms.الْبَيِّنَةِ: the legal proof or evidentiary establishment required in judgment
key_terms.لِحَافٍ وَاحِدٍ: a single covering or blanket under which the man and woman are found

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man and woman found together in one covering, and when is rajm established?
ai.summary: This report addresses a legal ruling concerning a man and woman found together under one covering, and distinguishes between flogging and rajm. It also clarifies that rajm requires the testimony of four witnesses who directly witnessed intercourse, while the compiler explains how the reports are to be reconciled in legal application.
